Name: John of the Cross
Summary: Spanish Carmelite friar, priest, and poet (1542-1591) who, with Teresa of Avila, reformed the Carmelite order and wrote the classic poetry of the soul's journey to God.
Contribution: He helped found the Discalced Carmelites, endured imprisonment by opponents of the reform, and wrote poems and commentaries on the dark night of the soul that have guided Christian prayer and mysticism ever since.
KeyWorks: Dark Night of the Soul; Spiritual Canticle
Testimony: Imprisoned and beaten for his part in the reform, he wrote some of his greatest poetry in a cell, trusting God in darkness.
